clue.text: Tried to get recipe to go in cooker

indicators.note: one thing going in another means it is placed inside, so the abbreviation sits within the appliance

blocks.note: a kitchen appliance for cooking
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe, 'take'

explanation.surface: A cook struggles to fit a recipe into their oven.
explanation.walkthrough: R for recipe is the old prescription abbreviation, seen on chemists' labels.
explanation.definitionFit: Strove is the past tense of strive, meaning made an effort or attempted hard.

clue.text: From whom one may need to be rescued

definitions.text: From whom one may need to be rescued

blocks.clueFragment: From whom one may need to be rescued
blocks.note: surface reading: a kidnapper, a fire or some other danger
setter's reading: a young innocent saved from the advances of someone luring them astray

explanation.walkthrough: The rescue suggests physical danger, but the threat is moral: the villain of melodrama who leads the heroine astray.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tempts another into wrongdoing, especially sexually, is the classic villain heroines are rescued from.

clue.text: Venerable object held by Roman priest

indicators.note: being held by something means sitting inside its grip, so the priest goes within

blocks.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic
Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A Catholic priest guards a sacred object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman priest' looks like one person, but it splits into the Catholic abbreviation and the biblical priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a saint's remains or belongings, kept and venerated as holy.

clue.text: Colour of lubricant swallowed up by pests

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading from bottom to top, so the lubricant runs backwards
something swallowed ends up inside, so the pests surround the lubricant

blocks.note: oil is a lubricant
vermin are pests such as rats

explanation.surface: Rats lap up spilled grease, painting a colourful scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermilion is a brilliant red pigment and the shade named after it.

clue.text: Army officer around  in the Mediterranean?

definitions.note: a description of where the island lies, standing for its name

blocks.note: an army rank above captain
ca is the abbreviation of circa, Latin for around

explanation.surface: A major is posted somewhere around the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like it wants to put one piece round another, but here it simply supplies the circa abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Majorca is the largest Balearic island, situated in the western Mediterranean Sea off Spain.

clue.text: Virgin clasped child in brotherhood

indicators.note: clasping something means holding it in one's arms, so the Virgin surrounds the child

blocks.note: the Virgin Mary
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A Madonna and Child image, set within a religious order.
explanation.walkthrough: The brotherhood is the Freemasons, whose fraternity is often called masonry.
explanation.definitionFit: Masonry, short for freemasonry, is the secretive fraternal society of Freemasons.

clue.text: He may be slapdash in assembling

definitions.text: He may be slapdash in assembling

blocks.clueFragment: He may be slapdash in assembling
blocks.note: surface reading: a careless worker putting something together
setter's reading: the word that precedes 'built' in the phrase for flimsy, cheaply put-up houses

explanation.walkthrough: Jerry-built means cheaply and shoddily constructed; the clue treats the first part of the phrase as a builder's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerry-builder throws up houses badly, so the man in the phrase is a byword for shoddy construction.

clue.text: Artist keeps trademark during new term

indicators.note: a new version of a word is a remade one, so its letters are rearranged
something during a period falls within it, so the trademark sits inside

blocks.note: taken as written
a brand is a trademark

explanation.surface: A painter retains his signature style throughout the new academic term.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt van Rijn was the great Dutch painter of the seventeenth century.

clue.text: A taste one has for a rodent

blocks.note: taken as written
goût is French for taste
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone has a liking for a small animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The agouti is a burrowing South American rodent related to the guinea pig.

clue.text: Not ultimately the good cooked meal

indicators.note: not at the end means the final letter of the next word is dropped
cooked food is altered from its raw state, so these letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, before its last letter goes
taken as written

explanation.surface: Not quite the hearty cooked dinner one hoped for.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot dog, a sausage in a bun, makes a quick snack or light meal.

clue.text: Angered about obligations incurred when high

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the word for angered is read backwards

blocks.note: riled means annoyed or angered
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts incurred

explanation.surface: Someone ran up debts while intoxicated and is now furious about them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being high, whether from drugs or excitement, is a wildly excited state like being delirious with fever or joy.

clue.text: He could be nothing more than a lady-killer

indicators.note: something that could be something else is a possible rearrangement, so these letters may be reordered

blocks.note: the round zero symbol for nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man is said to be no more than a womaniser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing more than' reads as a dismissive idiom, but it splits into the fodder and the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo, after Shakespeare's lover, is a common name for a man who pursues and charms many women.

clue.text: They could be prickly about theatre opening

blocks.note: c is short for circa, about
Act I opens a play in the theatre

explanation.surface: People turn prickly at a theatre's opening night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They could be prickly' sounds like touchy people, but the definition describes spiny plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert plants of this family typically bear sharp spines, so prickliness is their best-known trait.

clue.text: Little boy once got 4 for a tanner

blocks.note: first meaning: an old word for an urchin or small boy
second meaning: an old coin worth three halfpence, four of which made sixpence

explanation.walkthrough: A tanner is old British slang for a sixpence coin; the 4 is a number here, not a cross-reference to another entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic word named both a little fellow and a small coin of three halfpence, four making sixpence.

clue.text: What to do at university?

blocks.note: a question about how to spend student life
British students say they study a subject by this verb, and the same word names a university town

explanation.walkthrough: Britons say they are 'reading history' at university; the word is also a Berkshire town with its own university.
explanation.definitionFit: Studying a subject for a degree is described in British usage with this verb, as in reading law.

clue.text: About time to change aircraft accessory

indicators.note: going about something means encircling it, so the verb surrounds the word for time

blocks.note: to alter is to change
taken as written

explanation.surface: It's high time an aeroplane part was replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About time' reads as an impatient idiom, but 'About' is the instruction to wrap round.
explanation.definitionFit: An altimeter is the cockpit instrument showing an aircraft's height above sea level.

clue.text: The old chaps one may find in Aden

blocks.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
chaps are men
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Some old fellows might turn up in a Red Sea port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' does double duty, giving its numeral and also standing for the person in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a port city in Yemen, so a native of that country is someone found there.

clue.text: It's de rigueur to be male and right-wing

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
taken as written
being right-wing is being a Tory, a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A dress code insists on men who vote Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Something de rigueur is required by etiquette or custom, so it is obligatory.

clue.text: Debilitated by careless action

indicators.note: something done carelessly is sloppy and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has been weakened by a reckless deed.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine an atonic muscle lacks normal tone, so it is weak, slack and enfeebled.

clue.text: Saintly snob?

blocks.note: surface reading: a pious person who looks down on others
setter's reading: snob is an old word for a cobbler, so this is the patron saint of shoemakers

explanation.walkthrough: Snob once meant a shoemaker; the saint is the patron of cobblers, remembered on St Crispin's Day.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Crispin is the patron of cobblers and leatherworkers, for whom snob was an old name.

clue.text: War leader influences fashion

blocks.note: wins over, persuades
ton is a dated word for fashion or style

explanation.surface: A military commander sets trends in style.
explanation.walkthrough: Ton, borrowed from French, means the fashionable set or style; Winston Churchill led Britain in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill was Britain's prime minister through most of the Second World War.

clue.text: Cart came first without a horse

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the victory word goes round the rest

blocks.note: winning is coming first
a plus gee-gee, a child's word for horse

explanation.surface: The cart arrived ahead, though nothing was pulling it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a horse' suggests something missing, but 'without' means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: A waggon, the older British spelling of wagon, is a four-wheeled cart for heavy loads.

clue.text: Subject of a put-up job?

blocks.note: surface reading: the victim of a frame-up or rigged scheme
setter's reading: someone put up as a candidate for a post

explanation.walkthrough: A put-up job is a fraud, but here put up means proposed for election or appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is a person proposed as a candidate for an office, post or award.

clue.text: It might help to keep a cool head?

definitions.text: It might help to keep a cool head?

blocks.clueFragment: It might help to keep a cool head?
blocks.note: surface reading: something that helps a person stay calm
setter's reading: the frozen covering at the top of the globe

explanation.walkthrough: Keeping a cool head means staying calm, but here the head is the top of a planet, kept frozen.
explanation.definitionFit: Permanent polar ice covers the top of the Earth like a cap on a head.

clue.text: Taking part in course with no student finishing?

indicators.note: having none of something means it is taken away from the word for ending

blocks.note: completing means finishing
L for learner, a crossword stand-in for student

explanation.surface: A runner on the racecourse who has no hope of making the finish line.
explanation.walkthrough: The L of a learner driver's plate is removed from the word for finishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Racers on a course are contending against each other, which is exactly what contestants do.

clue.text: Old law was strict

blocks.note: ex means former
an Act of Parliament is a law

explanation.surface: A former statute was severe.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact describes something rigorous and precise, allowing no deviation, just as strict does.

clue.text: Panic in jolly fashion

blocks.note: à la means in the fashion or style of
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: Fear spreads in a cheerful way.
explanation.walkthrough: Jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine; the French à la, 'in the fashion of', comes first even though it is printed last.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm as a noun is sudden fear or anxiety, a close synonym of panic.

clue.text: Have a fighter round as a friend

blocks.note: taken as written
a MiG is a Russian fighter plane
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Invite a boxer over to be a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fighter' suggests a boxer and 'round' a bout, but these are a jet and a ring shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend and is used informally in English as a word for a pal.

clue.text: It's contrived to act as service dress

indicators.note: contrived means artfully devised, so the letters are rearranged into something new

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A uniform is a put-up job designed for playing a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests the military, but here it is a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotta is a short surplice worn by choristers and clergy during church services.

clue.text: Position of a yes-man with a view to advancement

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: someone who always agrees is in favour of whatever is proposed
second meaning: a rise in rank or job

explanation.surface: A sycophant agrees with everything in the hope of getting on.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as PRO MOTION: a yes-man is for any motion put to a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Being raised to a higher rank at work is a step up in one's career.

clue.text: Educated woman's witty sally about a strait-laced type

indicators.note: going about something means surrounding it, so the joke wraps round the woman

blocks.note: a play on words is a witty remark
Rita is the heroine of the play and film Educating Rita

explanation.surface: A learned lady makes a quip at the expense of a prude.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is Willy Russell's play about a hairdresser who studies literature.
explanation.definitionFit: A Puritan, from the strict Protestant sect, now means anyone rigidly moral and disapproving of pleasure.

clue.text: First person's love rejected in India

definitions.note: a location, standing for the place name

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the god's name is read the other way

blocks.note: my is the first-person possessive
Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: A man's romance is spurned while he is out in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysore is a city and former princely state in the south of the Indian subcontinent.
